Zalando evolved Zalando Plus in 2024 from a paid membership to a free-to-join, points-based system rewarding customer loyalty, initially tested in Spain and expanded to France and Austria, with further rollout planned for 2025. The annual report also mentions increased accruals for the reimbursement of Zalando Plus subscription fees to customers at the beginning of 2025, included in "others" within other current non-financial liabilities.

- The programme change: from paid membership to free-to-join with a points-based system (Key intangible resources, [4], [5]).
- Points are earned through purchases and activities like newsletter subscriptions, unlocking four benefit levels (Group strategy, [1]).
- Rollout: tested in Spain, expanded to France and Austria in 2024, more markets in 2025 ([1], [6]).
- Accounting: the awards create a separate performance obligation providing a material right (Accounting policies, [2]).
- Year-end accrual: increased accruals for reimbursement of Zalando Plus subscription fees at the beginning of 2025, included in "others" (36.5m EUR) within other current non-financial liabilities (Notes 9.–26., [3]).

Turkcell - 2G licence extension fee: EUR 120 million (plus EUR 21.6 million of value-added taxes)

Both operators agreed to the same extension fee of EUR/€120 million (excluding VAT). They paid differently: Vodafone Turkey paid the extension fee in advance with a capital injection, whereas Turkcell paid in installments — an initial payment of EUR 81.6 million (down payment plus VAT) in TRY 1.7 billion during 2023, approximately half of the remaining installments (EUR 31.1 million) in TRY 1.1 billion in April 2024, with the remainder due within a year.
